key_insight: MOSS enables deployed autonomous agents to evolve by rewriting their own source-level harness (code) rather than only mutable text artifacts, allowing fixes to routing, hooks, and state invariants that previously required human updates.
problem_solved: Deployed agent systems are largely static and cannot fix recurring code-level failures (routing, hook ordering, state invariants); prior self-evolution work only changed text artifacts, leaving the harness unchanged and failures persistent until manual intervention.
method: Runtime monitoring and failure/behavior detection to identify actionable code-level issues in the agent harness.
Automated synthesis and source-level rewriting of harness code (routing, hooks, state management) to produce candidate patches.
Automated validation (unit/regression tests, sandboxed rollout, rollback) to ensure safety and preserve invariants before deployment.
impact: Permits continuous self-maintenance of agent fleets, reducing human-driven patch cycles and improving reliability and adaptability in production; requires robust validation and safety guardrails to be practical.

paper_title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
paper_authors: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, Xianzhang Jia, Wei Xue, Jun Song
